# Edit the .po (Poedit, Weblate, or a text editor) and run
# tools/po-para-catalogo.py. A test fails if the two drift apart.

#   @key          opens a message; everything until the next @key is the text
#   {1} {2} {3}   where the variable parts go (a path, a name, a number)
#   # at line start   a comment
#
# This file is NEVER executed. A dollar sign, a backtick or $(...) in here is
# text and stays text.
#
# A key missing from this file falls back to the English original, so a
# half-finished translation still says something readable.

@ambiente_32_bits
{1} is a 64-bit program, and the Windows environment it sits in was made
32-bit. A 32-bit Windows cannot run a 64-bit program. That is a rule of
Windows itself - it is not a fault of your computer, and not a fault of this
program.

An environment's width is chosen when it is created and cannot be changed
afterwards, so there is nothing for me to install here. The environment is
this folder:

{2}

The way round it: copy the program to a folder outside that one - your
Downloads, for instance - and open it from there. Then I use my own
environment, which is 64-bit.

@origem_zip
And that is almost certainly what happened here: this program was opened from
INSIDE a compressed folder. Opening it that way takes out only the file you
clicked, leaving behind everything that was next to it.

Save the whole compressed folder somewhere first — the Desktop is fine — open
it there so that all the files come out, and only then double-click the
program.

@pedir_envio
May I send this line to the community list?

{1}

That is it, the whole thing. Nothing else goes.

What it is for: when somebody else opens this same program, their Tandem
already knows what it needs and does not make them wait to find out. The more
people send, the less each one has to work out alone.

What does NOT leave here: a file name, a folder, your user name, the
computer's name, a network address, or a single line of log. The first column
is a fingerprint of the program's file - not of you, not of your machine - and
there is no way back from it to anything.

You decide now and can change it whenever you like:
  tandem enviar sim     or     tandem enviar nao

@portas_aviso_alto
NOTE: the USB device {1} landed on {2}, and a lot of old shop software only
  accepts COM1 to COM4. If the program says it cannot find the device, that is
  almost certainly why. To pin it to a low port:

      tandem portas fixar COM2 {1}

@portas_aviso_dialout
NOTE: your user is not in the "dialout" group, and without that the device
  shows up on the list and refuses to open. To fix it, once:

      sudo usermod -aG dialout {1}

  After that you have to log out of your account and back in.

@id_titulo
What a program sees when it ties a licence to this computer:

@id_vem_da_maquina
COMES FROM YOUR REAL MACHINE (the same as it would see under Windows)

@id_fabricante
manufacturer

@id_modelo
model

@id_placa_mae
motherboard

@id_processador
processor

@id_memoria
memory

@id_rede
network ({1})

@id_nao_vem
DOES NOT COME, AND CANNOT
    BIOS serial number         Wine always answers the same thing, identical
                               on every computer running Wine in the world
    disk serial number         the same{1}

  If the program refuses to activate, it almost certainly saw one of these.
  That is not a fault of your machine: it is Wine being honest about what it
  is. The one who can unblock it is the company that made the program.

@id_serial_de_fabrica

    factory serial number      Linux only lets the administrator read that
                               number, so Wine puts a fixed identifier for
                               this machine in its place

@id_fica_parado
HELD STILL, BECAUSE TANDEM HOLDS IT
  (these live inside the Windows environment and, without this, would change
   every time the environment was remade - the commonest cause of "activate
   again")

@id_serial_disco_c
C: drive serial

@id_wine_escolhe
Wine picks it by itself

@id_identificador_maquina
machine identifier

@id_ainda_nao_existe
does not exist yet

@id_productid
Windows ProductId

@id_productid_de_fabrica
The ProductId above is Wine's factory default, identical on every machine
  running Wine. Tandem does not invent another one: a Microsoft licence number
  is not something you manufacture.

@id_identidade_mudou
NOTE: this machine's identity has changed since the environment was created.
  That happens when Linux is reinstalled or the disk is cloned. It is the
  explanation for a program asking to be activated when nothing else changed.

@id_vistas_diferentes
NOTE: on a 64-bit machine Windows keeps two registries - one that 64-bit
  programs read and one that 32-bit programs read - and here the two hold
  different machine identifiers:

      a 64-bit program sees: {1}
      a 32-bit program sees: {2}

  To a program that ties its licence to the machine, that is two machines. If
  one of your programs keeps asking to be activated again, this is the line to
  show whoever supports it.

@id_varias_placas
NOTE: this machine has {1} network cards. Many programs use a card's number
  as part of the identity, and if one of them is Wi-Fi that goes on and off,
  the identity changes with it. Leave the network always on.

@botao_instalar_tudo
Install everything

@ajuda
Tandem - runs Windows programs, Android apps and Linux packages.

  Formats: .exe .msi  |  .apk .xapk .apks .apkm  |  .AppImage .jar
           .deb .rpm .flatpakref .snap  |  .sh .run

  tandem                      opens the panel
  tandem install <file>       installs/runs any of the nine formats
  tandem preparar             installs what is missing (Wine, Java, Android...)
  tandem programas [name]     lists and opens the installed programs
  tandem desinstalar [name]   removes an installed Windows program
  tandem android              opens the Android screen
  tandem doctor               diagnosis of the environment (what EXISTS)
  tandem autoteste            exercises it for real (what WORKS)
  tandem repair               reapplies the file associations
  tandem dados                shows your own files inside Windows
  tandem dados salvar         copies ONLY your files (quick and small)
  tandem dados restaurar [c]  puts your files back from a copy
  tandem backup [where]       saves the Windows environment (a pen drive, say)
  tandem restore [file]       restores the Windows environment
  tandem protect <path>       protects a Wine profile from being changed
  tandem identidade           what a program sees of your machine (licences)
  tandem portas               pinpad, scale, printer: which COM they landed on
  tandem portas fixar <p> <d> pins a device to a port (e.g. COM2)
  tandem idioma [code]        which language Tandem speaks (pt_BR en es fr zh_CN hi ar)
  tandem alternativas <name>  looks for a Linux program that does the same job
  tandem receita <file>       exports what it learnt, to send to somebody
  tandem receita --importar <r> <file>      uses somebody else's recipe
  tandem memoria [name]       what Tandem has learnt about the programs
  tandem esquecer <name>      erases what it learnt about one program
  tandem lista                what the community has already worked out
  tandem lista atualizar      downloads the list (sends nothing of yours)
  tandem contribuir <file>    builds the line for you to send, if you want
  tandem enviar [sim|nao]     send what it learns automatically (default: sim)
  tandem socorro              gathers everything into one file to ask for help
  tandem logs                 shows the most recent log
  tandem version              shows the installed version
  tandem help                 shows this list

@faixa_de_ate
{1} to {2}

@envio_aviso_ligado
Tandem sends what it learns to the community list.

When you confirm that a program worked, ONE LINE goes out: a fingerprint of the
program's file, 32 or 64-bit, and which components did the job. Nothing else.

It carries no file name, no folder, no user name, no computer name, no network
address and no log line. The sieve that guarantees that runs twice.

This is ON. To turn it off, now or ever:

    tandem enviar nao

To see exactly what would go out for one program:  tandem contribuir <file>

@instalado_resumo
  Tandem installed.

    Double-click a .exe or .msi     -> runs on Windows (Wine)
    Double-click a .apk or .xapk    -> installs on Android
    Double-click a .AppImage        -> runs directly, nothing to install
    Double-click a .jar             -> runs on Java
    Double-click a .deb             -> installs, checking first
    Double-click a .rpm             -> explains why it is not for this system
    Applications menu -> Tandem     -> the panel, with everything

  Check the environment with:  tandem doctor

@chave_ja_roda
One thing in your favour: the {1} key service IS ALREADY running on this
  machine. So that is not what is missing. What is left to check is whether the
  key is plugged in, and whether the program is 64-bit — in that case there is a
  known fault where it claims "debugger detected" with no debugger present, and
  the company that made the program is who fixes it, not you and not Tandem.

@chave_nao_sei
I could not check whether the {1} key service is running here (this machine
  has no "ss" tool). If the program complains about a licence, that service is
  the first thing worth checking.

@chave_nao_roda
And I found the likely reason: the {1} key service is NOT running on this
  machine. It is the one that talks to the USB key from the Linux side — without
  it, the program looks for the licence and finds nothing, exactly as it would
  with the key unplugged.

  A technician installs it, once, and it is free: look for
  "{2}" on the manufacturer's site.

@portas_usb_rotulo

@vm_cabe_bios
This computer has the feature, but it is SWITCHED OFF in the BIOS. Turning it
  on means entering the BIOS as the machine starts and looking for
  "virtualization", "VT-x" or "SVM". It installs nothing and erases nothing.

@vm_cabe_apertado
This computer can take it, but only just: it has {1} of memory and {2} free on
  disk. The Windows inside wants about 4 GB of memory and 32 GB of disk for
  itself.

@vm_cabe_bem
This computer can take it: it has {1} of memory and {2} free on disk.

@vm_texto
There is a heavier road, and for a case like this one it works:

  run a REAL Windows inside Linux, and let only the program's window appear
  here on your screen, as if it were a program from here. The two programs that
  do this are WinBoat and WinApps, both free. Because it is a real Windows, a
  system driver works, and the USB protection key can be handed over to it.

  {1}

  What it costs, and it is better to know beforehand: you need a Windows
  licence, and it has to be the Pro edition — Home will not do, because it does
  not let the window out. And the Windows inside takes up disk and memory the
  whole time.

  Tandem does not install this and will not: it is a different kind of program.
  But it would have been dishonest to say "there is no way" without saying that
  this way exists.

@contrib_texto
Contributing to the community list

This is the whole line that leaves here. There is nothing else:

{1}

What each piece means:
  1. a fingerprint OF THE FILE (size + beginning + end). The same on any
     machine in the world holding that same file. There is no way back from
     it to the file, not even for you.
  2. 32 or 64 bits, read from the program itself.
  3. the Windows components that fixed it.
  4. the ones that were installed and did not fix it.
  5. whether you confirmed it worked, or only that it opened without error.
  6. a machine count (always 1 here; adding up is the list's job).
  7. year and month. No day, because a day identifies.

What does NOT leave here: a file name, a folder, your user name, the computer's
name, a network address, or a single line of log.

Copy the line above and send it to:
https://github.com/ChrnX0/Tandem/issues

@lista_ainda_nao_baixada

machines: which Windows components each program needed. Downloading it sends
nothing of yours anywhere.
